title: Erdős #65 OQ3: Liu-Montgomery Sharp Cycle Length Constant
description: The sharp constant in the GKS theorem is 1/2: for graphs with n vertices and kn edges, sum of reciprocals of cycle lengths >= (1/2 - o(1)) log k. Optimal, achieved by K_{n,n}.

meta.author: Hong Liu, Richard Montgomery, Gyárfás, Komlós, Szemerédi
meta.assumptions: 1 axiom (Liu-Montgomery sharp bound) and 3 sorries (harmonic sum bounds, optimality).

overview.historicalContext: The Gyarfas-Komlos-Szemeredi theorem (1984) proved that Sigma 1/a_i >= c log k for dense graphs. Liu and Montgomery (2023) determined the sharp constant c = 1/2, matching the bound achieved by complete bipartite graphs.
overview.problemStatement: Formalize the Liu-Montgomery sharp constant 1/2 in the GKS cycle length theorem.
overview.text: Sharp constant for cycle length reciprocal sums in dense graphs.
overview.proofStrategy: Axiomatize the Liu-Montgomery bound. Express bipartite cycle structure via harmonic numbers. Show K_{n,n} achieves the asymptotic constant 1/2.
keyInsights: Complete bipartite K_{r,s} has cycle lengths {4,6,...,2 min(r,s)} - all even
The bipartite reciprocal sum is (1/2)(H_{min(r,s)} - 1) via harmonic numbers
The constant 1/2 cannot be improved because K_{n,n} achieves it
prerequisites: Harmonic numbers and their logarithmic bounds

conclusion.summary: Formalizes the Liu-Montgomery sharp GKS constant. 1 axiom, 3 sorries (routine analysis).
openQuestions: Prove the harmonic sum bounds from Mathlib
Construct K_{n,n} explicitly to show optimality

crossReferences.description: Sharp constant for the main GKS theorem
